records.title: Long-Term PM2.5 Exposure Promoted Vascular Calcification through XBP1s-Associated Osteogenic Switching and Inflammatory Crosstalk.
records.abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a major environmental risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the mechanisms underlying long-term exposure-induced vascular calcification remain incompletely understood. Whether PM2.5 directly participates in mineral nucleation remains unclear. We found that PM2.5 accelerated the transformation of amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) into crystalline hydroxyapatite (HAP) and may act as a heterogeneous nucleation interface under simulated physiological conditions. Mice were exposed to environmentally relevant PM2.5 concentrations (5 or 35 μg/m3) for 180 days using a whole-body inhalation system. Long-term PM2.5 exposure increased arterial stiffness and promoted vascular remodeling and calcification. Mechanistically, PM2.5 increased XBP1s expression in mouse aortic smooth muscle cells (MOVAS), promoting proliferative and osteogenic phenotypic switching. Genetic deletion of Xbp1 markedly attenuated PM2.5-induced MOVAS proliferation, migration, osteogenic transformation, and mineralization. In addition, PM2.5-stimulated MOVAS acquired a pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype that promoted macrophage recruitment and M1 polarization, whereas Xbp1 deficiency attenuated these effects. We also established a human iPSC-derived blood vessel organoid (BVO)-macrophage coculture system and found that macrophages substantially amplified PM2.5-induced osteogenic remodeling and calcification. Collectively, these findings revealed the involvement of both physicochemical mineralization and XBP1-associated osteogenic and inflammatory responses in PM2.5-induced vascular calcification, providing new insights into the mechanisms underlying PM2.5-associated vascular injury.

records.title: Organoid-Based Strategy for Exploration of Cancer-Related Early Signatures of Low-Dose Methylmercury Exposure.
records.abstract: Methylmercury (MeHg) compounds are classified as Group 2B agents, possibly carcinogenic to humans by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), and as Group C possible human carcinogens by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA), but the carcinogenic implications of environmentally relevant low-dose exposure remain unclear. Here, we established a population-informed organoid-based strategy to explore the potential of low-dose MeHg exposure leading to cancer incidence. A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)-based analysis revealed nonlinear associations of blood MeHg with overall cancer history with increased predicted cancer probability around 5.39 μg/L for MeHg. Liver organoid experiments showed that low-dose MeHg did not cause overt short-term cytotoxicity but induced DNA damage and stress-response signatures after prolonged exposure. Transcriptomic analysis further linked low-dose MeHg exposure to cancer-related stress pathways, including reactive oxygen species (ROS) associated chemical carcinogenesis, p53 signaling, DNA repair, mitochondrial stress, and cell-cycle regulation. These results indicate that low-dose MeHg exposure could trigger early biological responses related to cancer-associated processes before apparent cytotoxicity occurs. This study supports organoid models as a human-relevant strategy for linking population exposure signals with tissue-level toxicological evidence in MeHg research and provides a potentially adaptable framework for evaluating subtle health effects of low-dose environmental pollutants.

records.title: Toward Dynamic Biointerface Toxicology of Micro- and Nanoplastics Using Organoids and Organ-on-a-Chip Models.
records.abstract: Micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) toxicity depends on the exposure conditions under which particles encounter biological tissues, yet nominal material descriptors alone do not resolve these conditions. Environmental transformation, biomolecular adsorption, aggregation, and chemical release can alter particle delivery and biological interactions. This Review evaluates these processes alongside evidence from organoids and organ-on-a-chip models, distinguishing direct MNP findings from analogue studies and demonstrations of platform capability. We propose exposure identity as an analytical framework connecting particle history and state with tissue encounter and subsequent processing over time. The synthesis examines what available studies establish about tissue access, barrier responses, distal relay, and susceptibility, and where interpretation remains constrained by exposure characterization or unresolved mechanisms. Human-derived models provide opportunities to investigate tissue-specific responses, but neither biological complexity nor perfusion establishes environmental representativeness or predictive validity. We identify measurement and control requirements for separating particle transfer from chemical release and tissue-derived signaling, interpreting absent effects, and evaluating heterogeneous exposures. Priorities include traceable delivered-dose measurements, synchronized exposure and response sampling, targeted mechanistic tests, and independent validation for a defined use. The proposed framework organizes evidence and testable relationships while retaining uncertainty about generalization to human exposure and health outcomes.

records.title: Bibliometric Visualization of Research Hotspots and Emerging Trends in Helicobacter pylori Research: A CiteSpace and VOSViewer Analysis.
records.abstract: Helicobacter pylori infection remains a major global public health concern due to its role in gastric malignancy and rising antibiotic resistance, requiring a clear mapping of research trends to guide clinical strategies. A systematic retrieval of Chinese and English databases was conducted (CNKI, Wanfang Data, Web of Science) for articles published from January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2023. Bibliometric visualization and analysis were conducted using CiteSpace and VOSViewer. A total of 5,707 articles were included (2,707 Chinese; 3,000 English). Chinese output peaked in 2016-2018, while English-language publication volume remained relatively stable. China and the United States were the leading contributing countries, followed by Japan, Germany, and South Korea. Analysis of Chinese literature identified 983 keywords clustered into 11 groups (Q = 0.572; S = 0.830), with recent keyword hotspots on gut microbiota, drug resistance, and pediatric infection. English literature revealed 16 co-citation clusters (Q = 0.906; S = 0.980), highlighting emerging interest in vonoprazan-based therapy, cancer organoids, and precision oncology. Gut microbiota and antimicrobial resistance were persistent research themes across corpora. This bibliometric study maps global research on Helicobacter pylori from 2014-2023, identifying sustained focus on gastric cancer, antimicrobial resistance, and eradication strategies, and emerging fronts in microbiota modulation and precision-based therapies. Findings reflect publication and citation patterns rather than clinical efficacy. Strengthening international collaboration and integrating bibliometric insights with rigorous clinical research may help organize and advance future investigations.

records.title: Enzymatic Enrichment of Sensory Epithelia from Late-Stage Mouse Embryonic Stem Cell-Derived Inner Ear Organoids.
records.abstract: Stem cell-derived inner ear organoids provide a cost-effective and scalable source of inner ear tissues for developmental and regenerative studies. However, the presence of off-target cell populations, including muscle and mesenchymal cells, reduces the relative abundance of inner ear tissues within organoid aggregates. Previous single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies have demonstrated that sensory epithelial cells, comprising hair cells and supporting cells, account for approximately 4% of total cells in mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC)-derived inner ear organoids at days 16 and 21 of culture. Consequently, additional enrichment strategies, including manual dissection, fluorescence-activated cell sorting, and downstream bioinformatic filtering, are often required to isolate target cell populations, increasing experimental complexity and reducing sequencing efficiency. This protocol describes an enzymatic pretreatment method to selectively dissociate and remove non-epithelial tissues from late-stage mESC-derived inner ear organoids. Adapted from a previously published method for enriching organoid-derived otic vesicle-like structures at day 12 of culture, the protocol involves treating day 23 organoids with a collagenase/hyaluronidase blend. Gentle trituration at 15 min intervals during enzymatic digestion facilitates the separation of epithelial tissues from the underlying mesenchyme. The resulting organoid-derived sensory epithelial sheets and vesicles are isolated using a 35 µm cell strainer and can undergo further enzymatic dissociation for downstream applications, including scRNA-seq. This method provides a straightforward, accessible approach to enriching sensory epithelial populations and reducing off-target cell populations in late-stage mESC-derived inner ear organoids, thereby facilitating downstream molecular analyses.

records.title: Differential impact of dynein pathogenic variants on mitotic spindle organization and cortical organoid growth.
records.abstract: Mutations in the dynein heavy chain gene (DYNC1H1) cause a spectrum of neurological disorders, including malformations of cortical development (MCD) and spinal muscular atrophy with lower extremity predominance (SMALED). How these mutations differentially affect dynein functions in the nervous system, leading to distinct pathologies, remains unknown. Using patient-derived cortical organoids, we address how MCD- and SMALED-causing dynein mutations alter human cortical development. We show that MCD-associated mutations alter the growth of organoids, but that SMALED organoids are unaffected, consistent with the microcephaly phenotypes of individuals with MCD. These defects are mirrored by a large increase in apoptotic cell death in MCD organoids. MCD mutations - but not SMALED mutations - strongly affect radial glial progenitor divisions, by inducing severe mitotic spindle defects and leading to prolonged mitotic duration. Mitotic checkpoint inhibition alleviates mitotic delay but fails to prevent apoptosis, indicating that mitotic arrest is not the cause of cell death in MCD. These findings reveal how specific dynein mutations can distinctly disrupt cortical development, establishing mitotic spindle dysfunction and apoptosis as central mechanisms underlying dynein-related microcephaly.

records.title: MitoLODE: a virtual mitochondrion framework with knowledge graph priors for trajectory modeling and mechanistic perturbation analysis.
records.abstract: Mitochondria play a central role in the pathogenesis of major diseases. Tracking how they evolve under disease conditions is valuable for understanding pathological mechanisms and identifying intervention windows. Existing single-cell trajectory inference methods rely on pseudotime rather than a real temporal axis, and rarely model disease and control as independent trajectories. Virtual cell methods target one-shot drug perturbation responses and do not handle the continuous temporal evolution of disease phenotypes. To address these gaps, we propose a virtual mitochondrion research paradigm. We first curate and construct MitoKG, a mitochondria-specific heterogeneous knowledge graph integrated from five authoritative databases. MitoKG contains 2549 nodes of four types and 23 019 edges of five relation types. Building on these priors, we develop MitoLODE, a conditioned dual-trajectory neural ordinary differential equation framework. MitoLODE embeds graph priors and temporal features throughout encoding, continuous-time dynamics, and decoding, modeling disease and control evolution as two coupled paths. Benchmarked against eight baselines across four datasets covering Parkinson's disease, cardiac, and pancreatic differentiation, MitoLODE leads in most settings and remains robust under low-data regimes and extrapolation to unseen time points. Two synthetic datasets with known ground truth validate its trajectory recovery under controlled conditions. Building on the trained model, we design a gradient-guided perturbation procedure that identifies potential intervention targets aligned with known Parkinson's pathology. We develop MGMI, a large language model-based reasoning module that grounds model outputs in MitoKG nodes and turns them into confidence-graded mechanistic hypotheses, which nonetheless require experimental validation.

records.title: Virtual Knockout in the Era of Generative AI: From Intracellular Networks to Spatial and Cross-Modal Functional Simulations.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation data have enabled computational models that predict intervention-associated cellular responses. This narrative review organizes explicit gene-regulatory-network simulations, latent and compositional response models, graph, optimal-transport, and dynamical approaches, foundation-model representations, and emerging spatial or cross-modal settings through a virtual-knockout lens. We distinguish representation-level ablation from causal genetic intervention and separate held-out regimes for genes, cell types or contexts, perturbation combinations, chemical structures, and doses. We compare representative methods, experimental resources, metrics, and benchmark frameworks and operationally define a prospective holographic virtual cell by its modalities, regulatory and physical constraints, intervention-conditioned outputs with calibrated uncertainty, and prospective validation requirements. The holographic virtual cell and Design-Build-Test-Learn roadmap are presented as future-facing criteria rather than as an achieved clinical capability.

records.title: Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Flavonoid Production: from Flavanone Platforms to Tailored Derivatives.
records.abstract: Flavonoids are valuable plant polyphenols used in foods, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. However, their production is limited by the low abundance of many flavonoids in plants and the structural complexity that complicates chemical synthesis. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative, yet engineering requirements increase sharply from platform flavanones to oxidized and multiply tailored derivatives. This Review organizes recent advances according to product complexity, covering flavanones, oxidized flavones and flavonols, and methylated, glycosylated, and prenylated flavonoids. We examine the major constraints at each product level, including aromatic precursor and malonyl-CoA supply, enzyme activity and selectivity, redox and oxygen demands, and the regeneration of activated methyl, sugar, and prenyl donors. We further highlight the need to coordinate scaffold formation, oxidation, tailoring reactions, donor regeneration, and host metabolism rather than optimizing individual pathway steps independently. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategies for enzyme engineering, demand-responsive pathway regulation, automated design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles, and virtual-cell modeling are discussed. This product-complexity-oriented framework provides design principles for developing efficient, modular, and programmable microbial platforms for flavonoid biomanufacturing.

records.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction.
records.abstract: Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction's reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder's first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto 4-32 fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder's reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation's observed response to its nearest training response increases. We propose predicted-NN-distance, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, as a per-prediction confidence score. The score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.81 with PDC, close to the 0.88 obtained with the observed response. Thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across encoders and cell lines, and the score remains predictive of PDC for drug perturbations.

records.title: LeakageHunter-SCFM: Evidence-bounded dataset-lineage auditing for single-cell foundation model benchmarks.
records.abstract: To develop and evaluate LeakageHunter-SCFM, an evidence-bounded informatics framework for auditing dataset-lineage evidence and calibrating benchmark-independence claims in single-cell foundation model evaluation. LeakageHunter-SCFM extracts accessions, DOIs, URLs, and repository identifiers from manuscripts and related artifacts. The workflow canonicalizes resources, assigns dataset roles, constructs candidate overlap pairs, and applies claim ceilings before reviewer adjudication. We evaluated it in a curated development corpus, a locked retrospective external evaluation set, and a small prediction-blinded prospective proof-of-concept evaluation. The development workflow reduced 673 raw candidates to 84 filtered resource entries and 53 candidate overlap pairs. Prediction-visible reviewer forms agreed across all 140 retrospective evidence units; their historical labels yielded F1 0.842 across 132 binary-scored units. Independent prediction-blinded relabeling of all 140 units followed by third-assessor adjudication yielded precision 0.727, recall 0.667, specificity 0.910, and F1 0.696 across 136 binary-scored units. The seven-record, prediction-blinded proof of concept achieved recall 1.000 and precision 0.611 across 52 evidence units. All actionable-positive units came from one record. Restricting this analysis to full article bodies retained 50 units from five records and F1 0.759. Evidence-bounded lineage auditing supports biomedical foundation-model benchmark review by separating identifier overlap, actionable review priority, and confirmed exposure. LeakageHunter-SCFM provides a reproducible triage layer for lineage evidence and reserves claims about corpus membership and performance effects for direct supporting evidence.

records.title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
records.abstract: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

records.title: Selective suppression and biasing of chemokine receptors CCR9 and ACKR4 through targeting CCL25 with de novo miniproteins.
records.abstract: Chemokines and their receptors mediate cell migration and coordinate immune responses, while dysregulation can lead to inflammation. Therapeutic modulation of the chemokine signaling axis has proven difficult. Most drug discovery efforts target the receptors, whereas natural regulatory mechanisms modulate immune responses by directly binding to or modifying the chemokine ligands. Despite this insight, development of effective chemokine-directed modulators has remained elusive. Recent advances in de novo protein design offer an unprecedented opportunity to produce high-affinity binders that efficiently block protein-protein interactions. We implemented a computational workflow leveraging the BindCraft platform to generate miniprotein binders against CCL25, the chemokine ligand for the receptors CCR9 and ACKR4, and implicated in inflammatory bowel diseases. The unbiased development results in several miniproteins designed to block the receptor N-terminus from wrapping the chemokine and preventing productive engagement. Thus, these proteins suppress CCL25-mediated effector coupling and halt MOLT-4 lymphoblast migration. Another class of miniprotein, represented by VUP25111, is predicted to bind CCL25 along the chemokine β1 strand and retained receptor binding. This complex inhibited arrestin recruitment to CCR9, but not to ACKR4, indicating receptor specificity. Additionally, G protein recruitment to CCR9 was unimpeded by VUP25111, suggesting that the miniprotein biased the native agonist towards G proteins. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of differentially targeting CCL25 to suppress CCR9 signaling and new tools to resolve the structural basis of chemokine receptor activation and bias.

records.title: AI-driven strategies for Cas12 protein design and genome editing optimization.
records.abstract: The rise of the CRISPR-CAS system has greatly promoted the development of gene editing technology. Cas12, with its unique molecular characteristics, has become an important editing tool following Cas9. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied in Cas12-related research, ranging from protein structure optimization, target design to editing efficiency prediction and off-target risk assessment. AI has demonstrated great potential in enhancing system performance and discovering new mutants. Most of these models were trained and benchmarked in human cell lines, E. coli, or yeast, whereas only a subset of engineering strategies has been validated directly in plants, including soybean hairy roots, rice, and Populus. This mini-review summarizes the latest research progress of AI in the field of Cas12 protein optimization and functional prediction, discusses the opportunities and challenges in its application in plants, and provides new ideas for future AI-driven plant gene editing.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-guided open-source CRISPR tools for designer crops.
records.abstract: AI-guided protein design enables rational optimization of clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR) components. Das et al. harnessed the AI-designed OpenCRISPR-1 to create a suite of tools for plant gene editing. Their open-source platform, PlantOpenCRISPR-1, targets academic and translational use and could offer a more accessible option for researchers facing licensing barriers, highlighting open-source CRISPR's future potential.

records.title: Design of mini-protein binders targeting CD46 to enhance complement-dependent cytotoxicity.
records.abstract: The complement system exhibits a typical dual regulatory role. Aberrant activation of the complement system contributes to the development of autoimmune diseases, whereas excessive suppression of complement facilitates tumor progression. Cancer cells evade complement-mediated killing by overexpressing three key complement regulatory proteins, CD46, CD55, and CD59. Among them, CD46 has attracted substantial research attention owing to its marked overexpression in a range of hematological malignancies and solid tumors. By overexpressing CD46, cancer cells promote the degradation of C3b and C4b, thereby escaping complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC). CD46 ectodomain consists of four small complement control protein (CCP) domains, which provide a limited interfacial area for molecular interaction, posing certain challenges for binder design. In this study, we integrated deep learning-based backbone generation, sequence design, and complex structure prediction to design and screen a panel of mini-protein binders targeting the complement-binding domain of CD46. We further optimized the binding affinity of the lead mini-protein binder via the partial diffusion strategy, achieving a final affinity of 287.5 pM. CDC assays showed that the monomeric mini-protein binder and the trimeric affinity-optimized viral ligand Ad35K++ exhibit similar potency for enhancing rituximab (RTX)-mediated CDC effect. Biochemical experiments confirmed that the engineered mini-protein binder exhibits high binding specificity for CD46 and good thermal stability. In conclusion, these newly designed mini-protein binders show promise for further pharmaceutical development and clinical translation.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Design of Peptides with Custom Secondary Structure Motifs and Reduced Amino Acid Alphabets.
records.abstract: Proteins are highly diverse functional polymers where the specific sequence of amino acids, selected from a standard genetically encoded alphabet of 20 (C20), determines the structure and ultimately the function of the resulting folded protein. This standard alphabet has been identified to be nonrandomly distributed in physicochemical properties crucial to both structure formation and function, often referred to as coverage theory. While machine learning models have drastically improved protein structure prediction, success of protein design models lags structure prediction, particularly for custom secondary structure motifs and amino acid alphabets. Here, we therefore bridge contemporary biological theory with recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) to develop and evaluate a generative AI protein design model, trained on hundreds of thousands of proteins within the RCSB PDB, for custom secondary structure motifs using reduced amino acid alphabets (RAAs). Results indicate an overall success in designing novel proteins with desired secondary structure motifs for a broad range of amino acid alphabets and complexity of designs. Interestingly, for a substantial fraction of designs, ESMFold predicts a fold close to that of the target structure despite training only on physicochemical sequence space and secondary structure information. The development of this model advances research across multiple disciplines, from general scientific AI architecture development to protein design for biotechnology, astrobiology, and early-Earth evolutionary biology.

records.title: Aligning Molecules and Fragments in a Shared Embedding Space for Property-Aware Fragment Selection.
records.abstract: Fragment-based molecular design offers a chemically grounded strategy for exploring drug-like chemical space, yet identifying fragments that are both chemically feasible and relevant to a target property remains challenging. Fragment-level attribution is inherently ambiguous because each molecule contains multiple fragments and the same fragment can occur in molecular contexts with different property values. We introduce Molecule-Fragment Representation Alignment for Generation (M-FRAG), a property-aware framework that aligns molecules and fragments in a shared embedding space. M-FRAG organizes fragments according to their local relationships with parent molecules and their global distribution across molecular properties. Candidate fragments are then prioritized by their distance and distributional proximity to property-relevant molecular regions and used to guide reinforcement-learning-based molecular assembly. Across five docking-based multiobjective optimization tasks, M-FRAG improves the novel hit ratio by up to 58.00% over the strongest locally evaluated primary baseline and achieves the best Novel Top-5% docking scores for all five targets while maintaining strong novelty and chemical validity. These results establish embedding-space-guided fragment selection as an effective and traceable strategy for property-optimized molecular generation.

records.title: Validation of the Turkish version of the artificial intelligence attitude in radiology scale for patients.
records.abstract: BackgroundIn the context of the growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into radiology, AI-assisted systems are increasingly presented as tools for improving diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and clinical decision-making. Yet discussions of AI in radiology often focus on technical performance or clinician perspectives, while patients' attitudes toward these technologies remain less well understood.ObjectiveThis study aimed to cross-culturally adapt the Artificial Intelligence Attitude in Radiology Scale (AIARS) for patients into Turkish and evaluate the psychometric properties of the modified Turkish version among patients receiving radiology services.MethodsThis cross-sectional validation study included 659 adult patients aged 18-69 years (Mage = 34.50, SD = 11.21). The factor structure was examined using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Measurement invariance was tested across age groups, gender, and educational level using multi-group CFA.ResultsEFA supported a modified four-factor, 23-item structure derived from the original 39-item, five-factor AIARS. CFA confirmed that the four-factor model was a good fit for the data, χ2(224) = 640.16, p < .001, CFI = .985, TLI = .983, RMSEA = .075, 90% CI [.068, .082], SRMR = .072. The total scale demonstrated high internal consistency, with α = .87 and ω = .88. Test-retest reliability was excellent (total-scale ICC = .97, 95% CI [.94, .99]). Measurement invariance was supported across age, gender, and educational level.ConclusionThe modified Turkish version of the AIARS demonstrated acceptable psychometric performance at the total-scale level and may be used to assess patients' attitudes toward AI in radiology. However, the Worries and Ethical Concerns factor requires further evaluation.

records.title: From epithelial-mesenchymal transition to liquid biopsy: mechanisms of gastric cancer metastatic dissemination and circulating biomarker-guided anti-recurrence strategies.
records.abstract: Recurrence remains a major cause of death after curative-intent treatment of gastric cancer, and imaging may miss residual disease before macroscopic relapse. This narrative review links the biology of dissemination with circulating biomarkers and potential strategies for recurrence prevention within a gastric cancer-specific conceptual framework. We examine epithelial-mesenchymal transition and plasticity, circulating tumor cells, and pre-metastatic niche formation, with particular attention to diffuse-type tumors and peritoneal dissemination. We then assess circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and molecular residual disease (MRD) as indicators of tumor-derived DNA shedding and recurrence risk. These domains are biologically related but do not form an obligatory linear sequence: plasma ctDNA is not a direct measure of epithelial-mesenchymal transition or niche activity. Postoperative ctDNA positivity is associated with increased recurrence risk, whereas negative results require caution in low-shedding and isolated peritoneal disease. We distinguish established perioperative treatment benefits from MRD-guided escalation or de-escalation, for which no survival benefit has yet been shown in gastric cancer. HER2- and claudin-18.2-directed treatments are discussed in their tested disease settings and require appropriate target assessment independently of MRD status. Preclinical niche-directed approaches, including traditional Chinese medicine studies, provide hypotheses for further investigation. The framework links mechanistic and clinical research while separating prognostic validity from evidence that biomarker-guided intervention improves patient outcomes.

records.title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated immune escape in osteosarcoma: mechanisms, evidence gaps and translational priorities.
records.abstract: Osteosarcoma remains the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and young adults, characterized by an intricate tumor microenvironment (TME) and stagnant survival rates for metastatic disease. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as pivotal mediators of intercellular communication within this ecosystem. This review synthesizes how osteosarcoma-derived EVs orchestrate immune evasion and drive premetastatic niche (PMN) formation. We focus on the best-characterized tumor-immune axes-specifically tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), T lymphocytes, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs)-while cataloging unmapped territories (e.g., dendritic, NK, and B cells) as critical evidence gaps. We delineate the molecular mechanisms by which EV-encapsulated proteins and non-coding RNAs reprogram TAMs toward an immunosuppressive M2-like phenotype, attenuate T cell proliferation via EV-associated PD-L1/PD-1 interactions, and recruit PMN-MDSCs to establish a permissive lung microenvironment. Furthermore, we discuss the role of EVs in transferring multidrug resistance and promoting angiogenesis. While EV stability and their disease-associated molecular cargo position them as theoretical candidates for future liquid biopsy applications and therapeutic vehicles, critical gaps remain. Mechanistic plausibility is strong for limited tumor-immune circuits, yet human source attribution, standardized EV characterization, independent biomarker validation, and therapeutic translation remain major bottlenecks. Addressing these challenges is imperative for the clinical advancement of EV-based strategies in osteosarcoma.

records.title: Urinary Extracellular Vesicle Nucleic Acids as Potential Biomarkers for Liposarcoma.
records.abstract: The development of minimally invasive biomarkers for liposarcoma remains an unmet clinical need. Extracellular vesicles have emerged as a promising liquid biopsy platform, but most EV-based studies have largely focused on blood. Urinary extracellular vesicles remain underexplored despite the advantages of urine as a non-invasive and easily accessible sampling source. This paper investigates uEV-associated nucleic acids as potential LPS biomarkers. uEVs were isolated from urine samples collected, both from LPS patients and healthy donors using two methods-differential ultracentrifugation and a microfluidic device that enables size- and tetraspanin-dependent EV capture. Analysis of uEV-associated MDM2 and CDK4 DNA, together with a panel of LPS-associated microRNAs, revealed differences in nucleic acid abundance across the examined uEV fractions. MDM2 and CDK4 DNA were significantly enriched in patient-derived vesicles. The microfluidic device further demonstrated its uneven distribution across distinct uEV fractions. Together, these findings suggest that uEVs represent a feasible, non-invasive source of LPS biomarkers and underscore the importance of accounting for uEV heterogeneity in EV isolation approaches when evaluating candidate biomarkers for liquid biopsy.

records.title: Extracellular vesicle-associated proteins in viral myocarditis: surface topology, immune pathogenesis, and translational opportunities.
records.abstract: Viral myocarditis involves overlapping viral infection, immune-mediated injury, cardiomyocyte stress, and remodeling. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are increasingly investigated as mediators and biomarkers of these processes, but their interpretation and clinical translation depend on the identity and topology of associated proteins. This review examines EV-associated proteins, particularly membrane-associated and externally accessible proteins, as a framework for understanding viral dissemination, myocardial immune interactions, liquid biopsy, and therapeutic targeting. Direct mechanistic evidence is concentrated in coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3) models, where extracellular membrane-associated viral populations can facilitate non-lytic release, alter cellular tropism, permit entry into receptor-poor cells, and reduce susceptibility to neutralizing antibodies. Host receptors, HSP60, autophagy-associated LC3, viral capsid proteins, and EV cargo proteins offer distinct mechanistic and translational insights; these findings cannot automatically be extrapolated to other cardiotropic viruses. Candidate circulating EV-associated proteins and cardiomyocyte-associated EV capture markers show preliminary diagnostic promise, but current studies are limited by small cohorts, inconsistent disease definitions, sparse confirmation of viral etiology, insufficient particle characterization, and limited validation against clinically relevant disease controls. A key unresolved issue is protein topology: a protein detected in an EV-enriched lysate may be luminal, membrane-associated, externally accessible, or derived from co-isolated soluble proteins, lipoproteins, or virions. External epitope accessibility must be established before a candidate can be used for intact-EV capture or extracellular targeting. We distinguish direct myocarditis findings from evidence extrapolated from other disease models and assess EV-virion separation, particle identity, protein localization, cellular origin, immune recognition, and clinical validation. A protein-centered approach integrating orthogonal particle characterization, mechanistic perturbation, and prospective human studies is needed to determine whether EV-associated proteins can become clinically useful biomarkers or therapeutic targets in viral myocarditis.

records.title: Granzyme B as a predictive biomarker for therapeutic outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer patients undergoing anti-PD-1 therapy.
records.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have transformed the management of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, durable clinical benefit is restricted to a subset of patients, necessitating reliable, minimally invasive pharmacodynamic biomarkers to monitor treatment engagement and response. In this prospective observational study evaluating an expanded patient cohort overlapping with our previous reporting, 64 patients with advanced NSCLC receiving second-line nivolumab monotherapy and 30 healthy controls were analyzed. Peripheral blood samples were collected longitudinally at baseline (T0), 6-8 weeks (T1), and 14-16 weeks (T2) post-treatment initiation. Plasma Granzyme B (GrmB) concentrations (pg/mL) were quantified via ELISA, and cell subset-specific intracellular expression was characterized using multiparametric flow cytometry. Archival tumor tissue was evaluated for PD-L1 expression, tumor mutational burden, microsatellite instability, and TP53 status. Exploratory in-vitro experiments evaluated A549 and NCI-H23 cell lines exposed to direct nivolumab treatment (0-200 µg/mL). Longitudinal dynamics were evaluated using repeated-measures linear mixed-effects models with multiplicity adjustments, and survival outcomes (OS and PFS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier. Responders (R) demonstrated significantly higher baseline tumor PD-L1 expression compared to non-responders (NR). Flow cytometric immunophenotyping revealed dynamic expansions in responders, including a three-fold increase in CD3+CD56+ NKT-like cells, a two-fold increase in NK cells, a ten-fold elevation in CD8+Granzyme B+ T cells, and a 2.5-fold increase in proliferating Ki67+CD8+PD-1+ T cells. Circulating plasma Granzyme B concentrations were markedly elevated in responders compared to non-responders and healthy controls (P < 0.0001). In exploratory cell-line assays, direct nivolumab exposure increased Granzyme B secretion and expression in A549 and NCI-H23 cells without impacting short-term cell viability. While higher circulating Granzyme B trajectory correlated with superior progression-free and overall survival, multivariable Cox regression indicated that Granzyme B kinetics serve as a dynamic marker of active immune engagement rather than an independent pre-treatment predictive biomarker when adjusting for overall clinical response. Longitudinal monitoring of plasma Granzyme B kinetics and cytotoxic lymphocyte activation particularly CD3+CD56+ NKT-like and effector CD+ T-cell subsets provides a valuable non-invasive pharmacodynamic indicator of systemic anti-tumor immune activation during nivolumab therapy in advanced NSCLC.
